title: Roasted Aubergine with Pomegranate
subtitle: Charred aubergine with pomegranate seeds, fresh herbs and a sharp dressing
excerpt: Roasted aubergine with pomegranate seeds, fresh mint, flat-leaf parsley and a sharp pomegranate molasses dressing. A Middle Eastern-influenced salad that works warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Aubergine with pomegranate is a combination deeply rooted in Persian, Turkish and Levantine cooking, where both ingredients have been used for centuries. The pairing of sweet-sour pomegranate with smoky, creamy aubergine appears in dishes such as Persian mirza ghasemi and Turkish patlican salatasi. The version here adapts these traditions for a salad format suited to the contemporary British table.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the aubergine up to 2 hours ahead. Add pomegranate seeds and herbs just before serving.

content.text: Roasted aubergine with pomegranate is a dish where the combination of flavours counts for more than the technique. The aubergine should be roasted until completely soft and caramelised; undercooked aubergine is bitter and spongy. The pomegranate molasses dressing is sharp and slightly sweet and provides contrast to the rich, silky flesh.

Heat the oven to 200 C. Toss the aubergine cubes with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Spread on a baking tray in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until the aubergine is golden, collapsed and caramelised at the edges. It should smell sweet, not raw.

Whisk together {{pomegranate-molasses}} of pomegranate molasses, the extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, 0.25 tsp of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Tip the warm aubergine into a large bowl or onto a serving plate. Drizzle the dressing over. Scatter over the pomegranate seeds, torn mint and parsley. Serve immediately or leave to settle at room temperature for up to 2 hours.

items.fix: Aubergine must cook until completely collapsed and soft throughout; pull it when it looks overcooked by Western vegetable standards. The caramelisation is what removes the bitterness.

items.cause: Pomegranate molasses varies in acidity between brands.
items.fix: Add a teaspoon of honey to balance. Taste before adding any extra pomegranate molasses.

content.text: Aubergine and pomegranate is a classic Persian and Levantine pairing. Pomegranate molasses reached British shops from around 2005 and is now stocked in most large supermarkets. This salad suits a summer dinner or a winter mezze spread.
